item.title: Timi O Is Putting Massachusetts Rap on the Map
item.description: Olutimileyin Ogunjobi, a young, emerging, Massachusetts-born artist who goes by the stage name Timi O, is making a real effort to shift that narrative—away from the mistaken assumptions and away from the numbers.

item.title: Campbell Posts Third Shutout, BC Beats No. 5 Northeastern 1–0 in Overtime
item.description: BC women's hockey beat Northeastern 1–0 on Sunday afternoon, earning its first win against the Huskies this season. Grace Campbell earned her third shutout win of the season while putting up 38 saves.

item.title: Scott Cann Named New VP of Information Technology Services
item.description: With over 25 years of experience, Scott Cann will take over as the new vice president for Information Technology Services (ITS) effective April 1.

item.title: Angela Pitter Takes Care of Business, and Empowers Others To Do the Same
item.description: Whether she’s advising businesses on their digital presence or volunteering within the Newton community, entrepreneur and community leader Angela Pitter operates under the same mindset: if something can be made better, she will be the one to get it done.

item.title: FACES Hosts Vigil To Honor Victims of ICE Violence
item.description: FACES Council, Boston College’s student-run anti-racism organization, held a vigil to honor victims of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) operations across the nation on Friday afternoon.

item.title: “A Home for Students”: Reflecting on 20 Years of AADS at BC
item.description: “I think we're unique in that students see us, not just as a major—like I do feel like we are a community,” McGuffey said. “I feel like we are a home for students who may have a difficult time finding a home at BC.”

item.title: Journalists Warn of the Displacing Effects of Climate Change at Clough Center Event
item.description: From wildfires in California to eroding coastlines in southern India, climate change is increasingly displacing millions worldwide and forcing communities to reshape their understandings of migration, according to journalist Meera Subramanian.

item.title: ASO’s Fashion Show is a Love Letter to African Culture
item.description: On this Valentine’s Day, admiration, appreciation, and love for these cultures filled the air as the crowd roared with excitement for every model walking by.

item.title: Bradley and Luckerson Trace the History of Black Activism Through Protest and Journalism
item.description: Victor Luckerson first learned the importance of writing and storytelling to social activism as a student at the University of Alabama, where he grappled with racial tensions entrenched in the history of Montgomery, Ala.
